name: Douban
subcategory: books, film and music social cataloguing
tagline: Chinese social network for rating, reviewing and discussing books, films, music and events, with groups and lists layered on top.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Core site is free and ad-supported, with paid content products alongside it.

verdictSummary: Douban is not a feature, it is two decades of Chinese-language reviews, ratings, lists and group threads that exist nowhere else. An agent can absolutely build you a private catalogue with star ratings, tags, shelves and long-form review fields in an afternoon, and it will be pleasant to use. What it cannot build is the reason you open Douban: the rating distribution on an obscure 1990s film, the one group where people argue about it, the reviewer whose taste you have tracked for years. Metadata you can borrow from open sources, though coverage of Chinese-language titles gets thin fast outside Douban itself. Build the shelf, keep the account for the crowd.
coreLoopDIY: A local media catalogue where you add books, films and albums, rate them, tag them, write reviews, and browse your own shelves and stats.
requirements: A machine to run it on, Docker or Node
Optional metadata lookup via an open API key in .env, otherwise manual entry
Willingness to type in titles the open catalogues do not cover
whatYouLose: Aggregate ratings and the review corpus behind them, which is the actual product
Groups and threads, including the ones that function as niche forums
Discovery: what people with similar taste are reading and watching right now
Deep metadata coverage of Chinese-language books, films and music
Events, marketplaces and everything else bolted onto the social graph
moatNotes: The ratings are user-generated, which means the moat compounds with every year of use and cannot be seeded by a single person.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people do not pay Douban money, they pay it attention, which is harder to redirect. The site is the default reference for whether a Chinese-language book or film is any good, and the default place to find other people who care about it. A private catalogue satisfies the archival itch and nothing else: no second opinion, no argument, no stranger recommending the thing you did not know existed. That asymmetry is why the shelf app and the account coexist rather than compete.
notes: The shelf is a weekend build; the archive is not. The moat is twenty years of user-written ratings and reviews plus the groups that formed around them.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted personal media catalogue for books, films, TV and music. Call it Shelf.

Stack, no substitutions: SvelteKit with TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling. Single Node process, no external services, no auth, no telemetry. Ships with a Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml.

Data model: items (id, type of book|film|tv|album, title, original_title, creators, year, cover_path, external_ids JSON, notes), entries (item_id, status of wishlist|in_progress|done|abandoned, rating 1 to 10 allowing half steps, started_on, finished_on, review markdown, private boolean), tags (many-to-many with items), rewatches (item_id, date, note) so repeat viewings are first-class.

Features in scope:
- Add item manually, or look up metadata by title using Open Library for books and TMDB for film and TV. API keys in .env, both optional. If a lookup fails or returns nothing, fall through to a blank manual form without complaining.
- Cover images downloaded once into a local ./data/covers directory, never hotlinked.
- Shelves view per type with filters on status, tag, rating range and year, plus a text search across title, original_title, creators and review body using SQLite FTS5.
- Item page with the review in markdown, rating history, rewatch log.
- Stats page: items per year, rating histogram, average by type, longest gap between start and finish, top tags.
- Import from a CSV with columns type,title,year,rating,status,finished_on,review,tags. Also accept a Douban or Letterboxd style export CSV by mapping whatever columns it finds and reporting the unmapped ones.
- Export everything to JSON and CSV from one button. This is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have.

Explicitly out of scope: user accounts, sharing, social feeds, aggregate ratings, recommendations, comments, mobile apps. This is one person's shelf.

Seed the database with eight varied example items so the UI is not empty on first run. Write a README with setup, the .env keys, and a plain sentence saying metadata coverage for non-English titles will be patchy.
